observations.statement: Deltas vs the no-binding baseline: passthrough adds +30.9/+38.7 ms of wall time per decode step (per pair), while the parent arm, which carries the same binding machinery plus candidate computation, is 3-4 ms per step faster than the baseline.

Run-to-run spread differs by arm: parent decode is tight (560.2-564.3 ms, ~0.7% spread), empty/direct spread ~3-5%, passthrough spreads ~12% (1693.8 vs 1904.2 ms). Only two pairs exist per comparison.

All runs passed quality checks; however passthrough is the only arm with nonzero max_abs_error (0.125 on both continuous steps of both pairs) while direct, empty and parent report 0.0. The cause of the numerical difference is not identified by this data.

hypotheses.claim: The passthrough decode regression is CPU-side Python dispatch overhead that becomes visible only in the launch-bound decode regime, not GPU work or candidate-side cost.
hypotheses.mechanism: Every aten op pays the ReplacementMode body (O10) and every module forward pays dispatch/signature work and, when site_parent is used, hook hashing and ContextVar tuple rebuilds (O11, O12). Local per-op costs (O15) times a per-forward op count in the low thousands bracket the observed +31-39 ms per decode step (O4). During prefill the same CPU work is pipelined under ~120 ms of saturated GPU compute, leaving only the observed +5.6-6.1 ms ttft residue (O3); decode steps end in sampling-induced synchronization, so CPU and GPU costs serialize and wall per step approaches CPU_overhead + GPU_step, matching 52.9-59.5 ms.
alternate_explanations: Revision differences between passthrough (bddbf75) and the baselines (O8) contributing adapter-level differences
Mode-induced changes in composite-op decomposition or backend selection also slowing GPU-side work (would also explain O6)
Per-step allocations (signature dicts, tuple concatenation) increasing GC pressure in the timed region

hypotheses.claim: Within the dispatch overhead, the dominant terms are the TorchDispatchMode interception floor plus tensor_description construction and linear signature-list scans at populated buckets, with hook sha256/tuple costs secondary.
hypotheses.mechanism: O15 ranks: mode floor ~6.2 us/op; bucket with signature work ~12.5 us/op; hook cost ~1.6 us/module. If functional specs exist for commonly executed ops, most ops in those buckets pay the full body; ops outside buckets pay the floor. Linear membership makes cost grow with observed signature diversity per site (K), which discovery accumulates per call id across shapes/steps.
alternate_explanations: If the bundle has no functional specs with site_parent, hooks are not installed (inputs/binding.py:142) and hook costs vanish
If all signature lists are short (K<=8), membership is minor and the mode floor dominates
If the bundle is module-only, no mode is created at all (inputs/binding.py:114) and the overhead must be attributed to module dispatch signatures alone

hypotheses.claim: The parent arm's net speedup over the baseline is candidate computational saving that exceeds the same binding overhead, implying the residual op stream seen by the mode in parent is much smaller than in passthrough.
hypotheses.mechanism: Parent carries the same install path minus candidate build (O9); the mode taxes only ops actually executed, and replacements that perform fewer aten ops shrink the taxed stream, while passthrough executes the full eager stream through the mode.
alternate_explanations: Revision differences between parent (0643ca5) and passthrough (bddbf75) bundles/spec sets (O8)
Different numbers of installed sites between the two bundles

hypotheses.claim: The nonzero passthrough max_abs_error (O6) originates from re-dispatch through the mode or from the revision change, not from passthrough substituting different math.
hypotheses.mechanism: Passthrough replacements call the original functions unchanged (inputs/binding.py:52-56, :57-60); remaining sources of numerical drift are composite-op re-dispatch under TorchDispatchMode or adapter differences at revision bddbf75.

hypotheses.claim: The higher run-to-run spread of the CPU-bound arms (passthrough ~12%, empty/direct 3-5% vs parent ~0.7%, O5) reflects host CPU contention sensitivity of Python dispatch work, not GPU variance.
hypotheses.mechanism: CPU-bound steps expose scheduler/GC jitter directly; GPU-bound steps (parent) hide it.

possible_generic_changes.change: Precompute the default parent ident once (module constant or session attribute) instead of hashing b"project.invoke|run" on every aten call executed outside any module.
preserves: identical parent value, so functional context matching unchanged
possible_generic_changes.expected_effect: removes ~0.6 us/op on stack-empty ops (O15); zero behavior change

possible_generic_changes.change: Cache module idents per (target, phase) in a dict captured by the hook closures; hash only on first encounter of a pair.
preserves: same ident sequence, same nested stack order (nested parent candidate semantics unchanged)
phase changes still produce distinct idents via the cache key
possible_generic_changes.expected_effect: removes the per-module-forward sha256 (~1.2 of the 1.57 us measured hook cost, O15); benefit scales with module count per forward
possible_generic_changes.risk: cache must be keyed on phase, not target alone, or idents would blur phases

possible_generic_changes.change: Replace the ContextVar tuple stack with a cons-cell stack ((ident, previous)); push allocates one 2-tuple, pop reads the tail, innermost parent is cell[0] instead of stack[-1].
preserves: LIFO order and immutable-update semantics of the ContextVar (async-safety unchanged)
same parent resolution for nested sites
possible_generic_changes.expected_effect: O(1) allocation per module forward instead of O(depth) tuple copy; modest (depth is small), stacks with C2
possible_generic_changes.risk: pop must use the exact pushed cell; exception paths already rely on always_call=True post-hooks pairing with pre-hooks

possible_generic_changes.change: Hoist signature construction out of the variant loop in module/project dispatch and make it lazy (compute once on the first module-kind variant, reuse across variants), mirroring the existing `signature is None` guard in the functional mode.
preserves: identical membership decisions and fallback accounting; only the number of tensor_description invocations changes
possible_generic_changes.expected_effect: removes 3.6-8.3 us per duplicate variant per module call (O15); helps sites with multiple specs on one physical owner

possible_generic_changes.change: Build, at install time, a per-spec membership set keyed by a canonical serialization of each entry of spec['signatures'] (e.g. transactions.canonical/identity at full digest length, or json.dumps(sort_keys=True)); replace the linear `signature in spec["signatures"]` with a key membership test, keeping spec['signatures'] as the declared authority.
possible_generic_changes.location: inputs/binding.py:106, :168; canonicalization exists at kernel_optimizer.project.transactions (identity = sha256 over sorted-key JSON, already used by discovery grouping at inputs/discovery.py:110, :207-211)
preserves: accepted signature set identical up to canonicalization fidelity; tensor_description output is JSON-safe (dicts with str keys, lists, str/bool/int/float/None), so canonical keys are faithful; spec['signatures'] stays authoritative and the set is derived
possible_generic_changes.expected_effect: membership drops from up to 15.5 us (K=128 miss) to a sub-microsecond probe (O15); largest win where sites accumulated many signatures
possible_generic_changes.risk: a canonicalization collision would wrongly match; using full untruncated digests keeps this at the same sha256-collision assumption the project already relies on for grouping; validate under M5c (bit-identical outputs and coverage)

possible_generic_changes.change: Key the functional index by the resolved op object instead of str(func) per call: resolve each functional spec['target'] to its OpOverload via the getattr walk already used in __init__, index by (op, phase, parent) with the object's identity/hash; keep a string-keyed fallback for targets that fail resolution.
preserves: same match set: OpOverload objects are process-stable and str(func) equals the stored target format (O16)
lookup order parent-specific-then-global and phase equality unchanged
possible_generic_changes.expected_effect: removes ~1.0 us/op of str(func) on every intercepted op (O15)
possible_generic_changes.risk: ops reached as different overload objects for the same string would previously collide by name; verify none of the bundle targets rely on that (M4)

possible_generic_changes.change: Micro-cleanups in the dispatch bodies: avoid `kwargs or {}` allocations when kwargs is None (call func(*args) directly), and hoist the diagnostic imports out of the per-call branch.
preserves: call semantics identical; kwargs-present behavior unchanged
possible_generic_changes.expected_effect: small (~0.1-0.3 us/op); included only because it is free

possible_generic_changes.change: Optional and more invasive, listed separately because it is not strictly local: enter the ReplacementMode only within phases where at least one functional spec could match (phase equality at inputs/binding.py:163 is the only phase gate), instead of around the whole adapter.run; hook registration windows would need the same gating.
preserves: matching cannot occur in phases with no functional specs, so scoping the mode to declared phases does not change which calls match, provided phase transitions are observable at entry
coverage counting unchanged for declared phases
possible_generic_changes.expected_effect: removes the ~6 us/op mode floor (O15) for ops in phases without functional candidates; the floor is otherwise irreducible because TorchDispatchMode intercepts every op
possible_generic_changes.risk: highest of the list: a missed phase transition would silently skip matching; requires explicit enumeration of phases present in specs and a guard that re-enters conservatively on unknown phases; adopt only if M3/M5 show the floor dominates after C1-C7

uncertainty.incomplete_comparison: The [parent, candidate] comparison has no candidate-side runs and no reverse-order pairs (O1). Nothing in this review should be read as a statement about the candidate's performance; the parent-vs-passthrough and direct-vs-empty contrasts are the only completed evidence.
uncertainty.attribution_is_hypothesis: The decomposition of the +31-39 ms/step passthrough overhead into mode floor, signature construction, membership scans and hook costs (H1, H2) is unproved until M2-M5 land; the per-op microsecond figures (O15) come from a different host CPU than the leased worker's, so only their ranking and order of magnitude are transferable.
uncertainty.unknown_bundle_shape: Number of functional specs, use of site_parent (hook gate), and signature-list lengths of bundle trial-09def220ed-param-def7baa6 are unknown (M4); several hypotheses (H2 alternates) hinge on these.
uncertainty.confounded_revisions: Passthrough runs at the candidate revision, parent at a different revision, baselines at the anchor (O8); any revision-level adapter difference is entangled with the measured contrasts, and the nonzero passthrough max_abs_error (O6) is unexplained (H4).
uncertainty.sample_size: Two pairs per comparison; passthrough's 12% pair spread (O5) means ratio estimates carry roughly that relative uncertainty; effects smaller than ~5% (e.g. the direct-vs-empty delta, O2) are within noise and were treated as null.
uncertainty.change_validation: Every proposed change (C1-C7, optionally C8) must be validated by unchanged quality checks, unchanged coverage counters (O14) and unchanged max_abs_error relative to the corresponding arm (M5c) before adoption; none has been implemented or executed in this review.
uncertainty.scope_limits: No routing-failure analysis, no search-policy modification, no model-specific matching rules and no per-failure action state machine are proposed; all changes are generic binding-mechanics changes evaluated against the stated invariants (signature/phase/context matching, nested parent candidate semantics, coverage).
